Subject: RFI follow-up: offline governance and build toolchain questions

Ben,

Thanks for the initial RFI package — we reviewed Appendix A and have two deeper asks before we proceed to procurement: one on build/toolchain compatibility for an air-gapped install, and another on signing/attestation for third-party components. High level: can Redwood provide a table that maps required build artifacts (container images, packages, packages with SBOMs) to the accepted delivery mechanisms for an offline install? Also, confirm whether Redwood supports HSM-backed package signing and whether your install process can consume vendor-signed artifacts without modifying them.

We'd like answers by EOD Friday (10-Aug) if possible. Cecilia will run the security review; I am coordinating procurement timelines.

Thanks,
Mike

Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: offline governance and build toolchain questions

Mike —

Appreciate the prompt. We put together a concise clarifications response and an artifact compatibility matrix (attached). High-level answers first:

- Delivery mechanisms: for offline installs we support (1) signed OCI images delivered on portable registries (tar archives), (2) signed tarball packages (RPM/DEB) with SBOM sidecars, (3) signed ZIP bundles containing runtime artifacts and operator manifests. The attached spreadsheet maps each Redwood artifact to the preferred offline transport and the verification steps we run on import.

- HSM / signing: Redwood supports validating vendor-signed artifacts using PKI chains; our installer can be configured to accept specific root CAs or vendor signatures. We also support optional integration with HSMs (PKCS#11) for signing during airgap staging if the customer provides the HSM or an HSM proxy during the staging window. We do not require modifying vendor-signed binaries — verification is signature-first, then optional re-signing into our internal attestations store.

- SBOMs & provenance: all third-party components include SPDX v2.2 SBOM sidecars. We produce an import-time provenance record (timestamp, hash, signature verification result) that can be exported to your audit system.

- Operator/tooling compatibility: our recommended offline toolchain is based on a curated subset of upstream tools; we list compatible versions and minimal checksums in Appendix B. We can also perform an on-site validation runbook and produce a signed runbook attestation for your auditors.

We're attaching two files: Redwood_RFI_AppendixB_tooling_matrix.xlsx and Redwood_Offline_Deployment_Crypto_signing_summary.pdf.

If helpful, Marissa (cc'd) can walk Cecilia through the attachment tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: offline governance and build toolchain questions

Cecilia / Mike —

Quick note on the HSM workflow we mentioned: for customers that require air-gapped signing without exposing private keys off-prem, we offer two patterns:

1) Customer-hosted HSM during staging: the customer brings a hardware HSM to the staging site (or provides an on-network HSM) and our staging operator performs signing operations in a controlled session. We produce an operational transcript and signed attestations.

2) Remote HSM proxy with attested channel: for customers that can host a small outbound-only ephemeral proxy during the staging window, the proxy provides signing via an HSM service in a way that still prevents bulk export of private keys; private keys never leave customer HSM.

On the SBOM side, note that some legacy vendor packages include incomplete license metadata — we annotate and produce a risk flag list. For any flagged component we can either (a) replace with a pinned, signed equivalent, (b) include compensating controls in the runbook, or (c) create an escrowed attestation package for your legal.

If you want to run a test import, we can schedule a 90-minute validation session next week. Vivek — can you confirm engineering's availability for a remote demo and sample import on Tue/Wed?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa / Ben / Athena team —

We can support a test import session on Tue 14-Aug at 09:00 PT (we'll reserve an engineering pair and a deployment engineer). What we'll validate in the session:

- Import of signed OCI image tarball and signature verification (cosign-based flow)
- SBOM ingestion and scan against license list (we'll surface risk flags)
- Verification of provisioning runbook (operator manifests) and idempotent install run
- Signing attestation generation and export to a customer-supplied SFTP/Azure Blob endpoint

Prep checklist: please share one sample signed OCI artifact (or a signed tar) and the corresponding signature key/cert or CA bundle (PEM). If you plan to use an HSM proxy pattern, include the network allowlist for the ephemeral proxy.

We will not accept private keys. We only require public certs for verification.

Looking forward — Vivek
